facts.raw_span: progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
no lymphadenopathy
routine hematologic tests were unremarkable
well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas involving the mandibular bodies, angles, ascending rami, and the maxillary tuberosities
bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar
no cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension
Vital signs were normal

concepts.why: The patient's symmetrical jaw swelling, multilocular radiolucent areas, and cortical thinning are consistent with Cherubism, a rare genetic disorder that affects the jaw bones.
The patient's bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates are consistent with Fibrous dysplasia, a condition where normal bone is replaced by fibrous tissue.
The patient's jaw swelling, multilocular radiolucent areas, and intact oral mucosa are consistent with Central giant cell granuloma, a rare benign tumor that affects the jaw bones.

The patient's multilocular radiolucent areas and cortical thinning could be consistent with Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism, a condition that affects bone metabolism, although the normal vital signs and unremarkable hematologic tests make this diagnosis less likely.

rationales.F02: Symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla is typical of Cherubism.
rationales.F06: Well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas are characteristic of Cherubism and Central giant cell granuloma.
rationales.F07: Bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates are typical of Cherubism and Central giant cell granuloma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The symmetrical, bilateral, and painless nature of the jaw swelling, along with the radiographic findings of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas, strongly supports Cherubism, which is a rare genetic disorder known for these characteristics, particularly in young children.
